A Stanford AI professor came up with a way to combine Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol into a unified setup, and this approach completely changes standard concepts of search structure

The professor's development completely eliminates human-created rigid search frameworks and separates intellectual labor into distinct layers:

Control module: Claude Opus 5.5 forms a search plan through queries to a persistent knowledge graph, where MCTS and MAP-Elites are transformed into direct Cypher queries

Candidate module: GPT-6.1 Sol explores high-entropy code modifications in secure execution environments

Context isolation: The context window is reset on every iteration to save tokens, while the full tree history is recorded in the graph

Independent evaluation: Candidate code is strictly separated from the validation system, preventing test data leakage and reward function manipulation

Opus sets the vector of movement along the graph, while Sol verifies hypotheses in code

posts.text:
Claude Code tip: stop burning Opus 5.5 context on tasks Sonnet 5.5 can swarm, while Fable 5.1 sits idle

spin up an autonomous team with --agent

claude --agent architect

Opus 5.5 acts as the lead architect, scoping the work and validating every worktree before it merges
Sonnet 5.5 teammates take isolated git worktrees and hammer out implementations at medium effort
Fable 5.1 sits on the team as a dedicated adversary, only stepping in at three critical moments:

→ before a contract locks: does the frontend payload match the backend schema?
→ when a test breaks twice: are we patching the bug or just hiding the symptom?
→ before the merge: what attack surface or edge case did everyone overlook?

Sonnet 5.5 builds. Fable 5.1 challenges. Opus 5.5 merges and ships

Jev engineering runs the identical pattern one layer down: mechanical decisions that need no reasoning (which file to open, which tool to invoke, retry or abort) execute in 16ms, so the frontier models only wake up when execution paths actually diverge

Plan on high. Delegate on medium. Keep the adversary on peer-to-peer call.

- the full team setup
> architect runs the main session on Opus 5.5 at high effort
> teammate-ux builds client state inside its own git worktree
> teammate-back writes endpoints and migrations inside a separate worktree
> teammate-adv runs on Fable 5.1, read-only, and attacks every diff
> teammates message each other by name without routing through the lead
> tools: Agent(ux, backend, adversary) locks the architect to spawning only its own team

paste the setup and this prompt into Claude Code below:

"Configure my Claude Code workspace for an autonomous agent team:

1. Audit ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents for definitions fitting architect, ux, backend and adversary
> Generate definitions only for missing roles
> Pin model: sonnet, effort: medium, isolation: worktree for ux and backend, and model: fable with read-only tools for adversary
> Give architect model: opus, effort: high and tools: Agent(ux, backend, adversary)

2. Check ~/.claude/settings.json and my env:
> Report CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS if it's set, since it turns named subagents into teammates without worktrees
> Report CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, which can override the pinned models and effort

3. Write each role's prompt so ux and backend own separate folders, message each other by name when a contract changes, and hand every diff to adversary before reporting back

4. Add a team rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: no worktree merges until adversary has reviewed it

Show every configuration diff first. Do not apply edits until confirmed"

save it

Claude Codeのコツ：Sonnet 5.5を群れで回せる作業にOpus 5.5のコンテキストを浪費しない。Fable 5.1も遊ばせない

--agentで自律チームを立ち上げる

claude --agent architect

Opus 5.5はリードアーキテクト。作業範囲を決め、各worktreeをマージ前に検証する
Sonnet 5.5のチームメイトは独立したgit worktreeを担当し、effort mediumで実装を進める
Fable 5.1は専任の反対役として、重要な3つの場面だけ登場する：

→ 契約を固める前：フロントのペイロードはバックエンドのスキーマと合っているか？

→ マージ前：全員が見落とした攻撃面やエッジケースは？

Sonnet 5.5が作り、Fable 5.1が突っ込み、Opus 5.5がマージして出荷する

Jevのエンジニアリングも1段下の層で同じパターン：推論が要らない機械的な判断（どのファイルを開くか、どのツールを呼ぶか、リトライか中止か）は16msで実行し、最先端モデルは実行経路が本当に分かれるときだけ起動する

計画はhigh、委任はmedium、反対役は常に対等に呼べるように。

- チーム構成の全体
> architect：メインセッション、Opus 5.5・effort high
> teammate-ux：自分のgit worktree内でクライアント状態を実装
> teammate-back：別のworktreeでエンドポイントとマイグレーションを書く
> teammate-adv：Fable 5.1、読み取り専用で全差分を攻める
> チームメイト同士はリードを経由せず名前で直接メッセージ
> tools: Agent(ux, backend, adversary) でarchitectが自チームだけを起動できるよう制限

以下の設定とプロンプトをClaude Codeに貼り付け：

「Claude Codeのワークスペースを自律エージェントチーム用に設定して：

1. ~/.claude/agents と .claude/agents から architect・ux・backend・adversary に合う定義を確認
> 足りない役割の定義だけ生成
> ux と backend は model: sonnet、effort: medium、isolation: worktree、adversary は model: fable で読み取り専用ツール
> architect は model: opus、effort: high、tools: Agent(ux, backend, adversary)

2. ~/.claude/settings.json と環境変数を確認：
> CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS が設定されていれば報告（名前付きサブエージェントがworktreeなしのチームメイトになるため）
> モデルやeffortの固定を上書きしうる CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE と CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL を報告

3. 各役割のプロンプトは、uxとbackendが別フォルダを担当し、契約が変わったら名前で連絡し合い、報告前に全差分をadversaryに渡すように書く

4. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md にチームルールを追加：adversaryのレビュー前にworktreeをマージしない

まず設定の差分をすべて見せて。確認するまで編集は適用しないこと」

𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗥𝗔𝗚 𝘃𝘀 𝗡𝗮𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗥𝗔𝗚 𝘃𝘀 𝗩𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗥𝗔𝗚.

𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗥𝗔𝗚 puts an agent in control of retrieval.

It can decompose a complex question into smaller searches, choose between retrieval tools, evaluate what comes back, refine its queries, and retrieve again when context is missing. Retrieval becomes an iterative reasoning loop rather than a single step.

With 𝗡𝗮𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗥𝗔𝗚 a simpler retrieval pipeline is used.

The query is embedded, similar chunks are retrieved from a vector database, and the most relevant results are added to the LLM’s context. There’s typically no reasoning loop deciding whether to search again or change the retrieval strategy.

Whereas 𝗩𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗥𝗔𝗚 challenges a different assumption: do you need vector search at all?

Instead of relying on embeddings and vector similarity, retrieval can use approaches like keyword search, document structure, graph traversal, or relational queries.

The difference isn’t which approach is “best.” It’s whether retrieval needs to be fixed or adaptive, and which retrieval method actually fits your data and queries.

Whichever approach you use, the fundamentals of retrieval still matter: how your data is prepared, how relevant context is found, and how that context reaches the model.

posts.textJa:
エージェント型RAG vs 素朴なRAG vs ベクトルレスRAG

エージェント型RAGは、検索の主導権をエージェントに持たせる。

複雑な質問を小さな検索に分解し、検索ツールを選び、結果を評価し、クエリを改善して、文脈が足りなければ再検索できる。検索が1回きりの処理ではなく、反復する推論ループになる。

素朴なRAGでは、よりシンプルな検索パイプラインを使う。

クエリを埋め込み、ベクトルDBから似たチャンクを取り出し、関連度の高い結果をLLMの文脈に加える。再検索や戦略変更を判断する推論ループは基本的にない。

一方ベクトルレスRAGは別の前提を問う：そもそもベクトル検索は必要か？

埋め込みやベクトル類似度に頼らず、キーワード検索、文書構造、グラフ探索、リレーショナルクエリなどで検索できる。

違いは「どれが最良か」ではない。検索を固定にすべきか適応的にすべきか、そしてデータとクエリに本当に合う方法はどれか、だ。

どの方式でも検索の基本は変わらない：データの準備方法、関連する文脈の見つけ方、その文脈をモデルにどう届けるか。
